subject: MAP: performance playbook & SLOs for Stellar HealthTech POC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@stellarhealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: performance playbook & SLOs for Stellar HealthTech POC

Alex — attaching a concise MAP appendix focused on the performance eval we'll run as part of the POC. High-level ask: confirm the workload samples and success criteria below so we can lock the test window next week.

Attachments: MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP timeline & responsibilities), workload-sample-traces.jsonl (anonymized prod traces)

Proposed benchmarking scope (short):
- Workload: mix of 65% single-turn generation, 25% short chat (2-3 turns), 10% embeddings/rerank. Input length distribution: 32 token median, 512 token tail.
- Concurrency targets: stable runs at 8/16/32 concurrent connections; stress window to 64 to observe degradation.
- Metrics to capture: latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT (time-to-first-token), throughput (req/s), GPU util, memory/KV cache pressure, error rate.
- Success criteria: p95 generation latency <= 300 ms at 16 concurrency; TTFT < 220 ms; end-to-end throughput >= 100 req/s sustained for 10m at 16 concurrency; error rate < 0.5%.
- Acceptance test: two production-like replay runs using your prod-sample traces (attached).

Timeline (MAP milestones):
- 6/11: agree workload & SLOs (this thread)
- 6/12–6/14: Redwood runs baseline + tuned runs (we'll use quantization and caching profiles)
- 6/15: delivery of raw results + CSV (benchmark-results-20260615.csv)
- 6/16: joint results review and go/no-go decision

Next steps:
1) Confirm the workload mix and that sample traces are representative.
2) Share any constraints (IP, PII) we need for the runs.

Thanks — will keep runs isolated to the POC model variants & provide a canary/rollback plan in the MAP.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: MAP: performance playbook & SLOs for Stellar HealthTech POC

Thanks Marcus — this looks good and thorough. Quick clarifications: 1) For concurrency, when you say 16 concurrency is that simultaneous open sessions or parallel requests? Our infra will simulate session affinity (long-lived connections). 2) We can provide prod-sample traces but want to strip patient identifiers — the attached JSONL looks anonymized.

Also, procurement wants any firm limits on resource commits before they sign the reserved capacity addendum. Can you call that out in the MAP?

I'll loop procurement once we agree on the SLOs. Otherwise green to proceed on 6/12.

—Alex
Alex Green
Head of Integrations, Stellar HealthTech
alex.green@stellarhealthtech.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@stellarhealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: performance playbook & SLOs for Stellar HealthTech POC

Alex — good questions. Short answers:
- Concurrency: we're measuring parallel in-flight requests across the serving cluster (so session-affinity counted as concurrent requests if they are actively generating). We'll include a session-affinity run to match your production pattern.
- Data: confirmed your file is anonymized; thanks. We will not persist raw payloads, only aggregated metrics and sampled token traces (no PII).
- Procurement: we'll add a short 'resource guardrail' section to the MAP that lists reserved GPU hours for the test window (estimate: 48 GPU-hours across tuned runs) and an upper bound on burst spend. That should be sufficient for procurement to proceed with a short addendum.

Updated success criteria (after sync with infra):
- p50 latency generation: <= 85 ms at 16 concurrency
- p95 latency generation: <= 300 ms at 16 concurrency
- TTFT: median < 120 ms, 95th < 220 ms
- Sustained throughput: >= 110 req/s for 10 continuous minutes at 16 concurrency
- Max tolerable error rate: 0.5% (errors or invalid outputs)
- Degradation threshold: if p95 > 450 ms or error rate > 2% at any run, we mark as fail and trigger rollback plan.

I'll update MAP_v1.2.pdf with the procurement guardrail and upload the results CSV after runs. Plan stands to run 6/12–6/14.

—Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@stellarhealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark results: Stellar HealthTech POC (raw + summary)

Folks — ran the three canonical runs (8/16/32 concurrency) using your anonymized traces with the tuned quantization profile and prefix caching enabled. Attached: benchmark-results-20260615.csv (raw), and a short summary below.

Summary (key numbers):
- 8 concurrency run:
  - p50 latency: 72 ms
  - p95 latency: 180 ms
  - TTFT median: 90 ms
  - sustained throughput: 95 req/s
  - error rate: 0.12%

- 16 concurrency run (primary acceptance target):
  - p50 latency: 83 ms
  - p95 latency: 290 ms
  - p99 latency: 520 ms (tail under stress)
  - TTFT median: 110 ms; TTFT 95th: 200 ms
  - sustained throughput: 118 req/s over 10m window
  - error rate: 0.4%

- 32 concurrency run (stress):
  - p50 latency: 140 ms
  - p95 latency: 610 ms (exceeds acceptable)
  - TTFT median: 190 ms
  - throughput: peaked at 190 req/s but instability observed after 6m
  - error rate: 1.8% (approaching degradation threshold)

Notes & recommended mitigations:
- The POC acceptance threshold (p95 <= 300 ms at 16 concurrency, TTFT95 <= 220 ms, throughput >= 110 req/s) is met for the 16 concurrency run.
- Stress above 16 shows queuing and KV cache pressure; recommend autoscaling to add capacity at 24–32 concurrency and enable additional KV sharding for production.
- Observed repeated ~10% variance in p99 tail for long outputs — possible kernel fallback under long sequence conditions. We can retune token-batching parameters and reduce tail latency.

Next steps:
- 6/16 10:00 PT: joint review (I added the meeting invite)
- If agreed, procurement addendum (48 GPU-hours + burst cap) and Dedicated capacity onboarding can proceed in parallel.

Full CSV and graphs are in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

—Marcus

From: Alex Green <alex.green@stellarhealthtech.com>

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the thorough summary and fast turnaround. Happy to confirm that the acceptance criteria are met for the 16-concurrency run. Procurement is looped and will review the guardrails + addendum.

Two asks before the review: 1) can you add a short paragraph to the MAP on rollback behavior and SLA implications if we exceed the stress thresholds; 2) please include an estimated timeline for Dedicated onboarding if we sign (ballpark lead time).

I'll see you on the review at 10am PT.

—Alex
